This CSS file provides the visual styling and layout rules for a local client application interface. It defines global base styles (font stack, color scheme, box-sizing, focus outlines) and a set of component and layout rules for the main application shell: a two-column layout with a fixed-width sidebar and a fluid main content area, a top bar, content panels, cards, forms, and utility pieces such as toasts and hidden elements. The stylesheet includes component-specific styling for branding, navigation, template cards, editor panels, document rows, and a variety of form and list patterns used across the app.

The file also contains responsive rules delivered through media queries to adapt the layout at common breakpoints (1080px and 760px). Many components use modern CSS layout primitives like flexbox and CSS grid, border-radius and subtle shadows for visual hierarchy, and consistent spacing and typography for readability. Several small utility and state classes (for example .active, .hidden, and :hover/:focus-visible states) are present to support interactive behavior driven by the application.

overview.summary:
This file implements a client-side application script responsible for the user-facing behavior of a local web client. It contains a large collection of module-level functions that perform API calls, manage view selection and location syncing, render and interact with template collections and previews, create pages from templates, manage document searches and loading, and control the in-browser editor lifecycle. Utility functions provide UI behavior such as toast notifications, select population, filter handling, unique value computation, and a handful of date and formatting helpers.

The module also registers global event handlers for window dragover, hashchange, and document keydown to integrate with browser events. Many functions are asynchronous where network or IO operations are required (for example api, selectView, openTemplatePreview, createPageFromTemplate, loadDocuments), while others are synchronous helpers for rendering and state updates. The file centralizes client-side interactions related to templates, documents, favorites, and editor operations used by the rest of the application.

overview.summary:
This module implements a wide set of client-side utilities and handlers for an in-browser page canvas used in a local client application. The functions manage canvas state and metadata (colors, tabs, mastheads, properties), editing workflows (draft persistence, dirty tracking, undo/redo, edit history), keyboard and clipboard interactions (shortcuts, copy/cut/paste), and UI rendering for workspace tabs and tags. Overall, it centralizes the logic for maintaining an editable page canvas, connecting UI rendering, user input handling, and draft persistence mechanisms.

overview.summary: This module implements a local, user-configurable database layer for storing custom databases, their properties, views, records and revision history. It defines Pydantic models for inputs and revisions (Input, Revision, DatabaseInput, DatabaseUpdate, PropertyInput, ViewConfig, ViewInput, RecordInput, RecordUpdate, RecordBatch) that represent the shapes of databases, properties, views and record payloads. A CustomDatabaseStore class encapsulates the operational logic for managing these entities and their histories. The module also exposes helper functions for common HTTP error responses and encoding/normalization utilities, as well as a mount_custom_databases function intended to attach the custom database API into a FastAPI application or router.
